text:
maria: Heads-up: were publishing a minor but important policy update to the Ruby SDK gem: were adopting strict semver for the gem (major.minor.patch) and a 30-day deprecation notice window for any breaking behavior flagged in patch releases. Docs + release notes will go out today. :gem:

henry: Quick Q: does this change how we bump minor releases for new features?

maria: Short answer: no. Minor bumps still contain new, backward-compatible features. Patch bumps must be patch-only (bug fixes) and must not introduce behavioral changes. If a breaking fix is unavoidable, it must be published as a new minor with a deprecation path documented, plus a 30-day note on the top of the Ruby SDK page.

henry: Eng plan: we'll add CI lint to validate changelog entries and a semantic check in release automation to block patch releases that reference breaking changes. Also adding a `--semver-check` job to release pipeline.

eli: Docs tasks: update the gem publishing guide, add a policy section "Ruby SDK semver and deprecation policy", and a short migration checklist for integrators. I'll add a banner to the Ruby SDK page and a templated email for customers. Draft by EOD.

support: Please provide a 2-line TL;DR for Support + suggested response template for customers who see a behavior change after a patch upgrade.

maria: TL;DR suggestion for support: 1) We now enforce strict semver for ruby gems; 2) If you see behavior changes from a patch, please upgrade to the pinned minor and contact support; include gem version and changelog link.

docs-bot: Published: docs PR #4477 by eli - "ruby: semver and deprecation policy + release automation checks (WIP)" (automated).

henry: Ops note: for Dedicated/Private, we'll pin the gem in runtime images for 12 months and provide a backport fix channel. We'll also surface a runtime warning when a non-pinned patch is installed.

maria: Thanks everyone. Action items: henry -> release CI checks; eli -> docs + email template; support -> short script and FAQ entry. Ping me if you find edge cases in existing releases. :thumbsup:
